go up, a slow disbelieving smile. On the last word she tilts her head and begins to lean in; her eyes start to close.

his cheekbone — and a huge blissful smile, his lips puckering and stretching upward toward nothing, his chin
lifting a little off the ground.

staring down at his puckered lips — brows knitted, mouth half open, head tilting slowly to one side: completely

and he lets go, hands up in the air, apologising in a rush.

sitting side by side on the asphalt — Ryan at screen-left, hand at his temple, Enjee at screen-right, turned toward
him. Hold.

ACTING TASK — RYAN (fully invested in his tactic; the work happens in his eyes)
SCENE DIRECTION (shared, unspoken): in the dream — let it happen; in reality — survive the embarrassment.
MOTIVE (his fuel): the last thing he knows is a red jacket and a fist; the thing his mind gives him instead is
everything he has never let himself want out loud.
GOAL: in the dream, to be kissed by her; awake, to undo the last five seconds.
OBSTACLE: the dream is not real, and the girl in his arms is.
TACTIC: in the dream he does nothing to deserve it and cannot believe it — he only lets it arrive, wide-eyed, then
closes his eyes and pulls her in. Awake, he understands everything in one look at her face and lets go as if she
were hot, and the apology comes out too fast, too many times.
Moment to moment:
— "You're the bravest…" — disbelief, then the melt.
— the pucker in reality — blissful, ridiculous, unaware.
— the pull in the dream — his hands at her waist.
— the voice — eyes snap open.
— the reveal — a frozen stare at her face above his.
— letting go — hands up, fast.
— "Sorry — sorry! I — sorry." — mortified, to her eyes and away.
— sitting up — the head throbs; the wince; the glasses on crooked.
(Safety: gaze always engaged in the task — never a frozen, glassy stare; natural blink cadence.)

ACTING TASK — ENJEE, REALITY (fully invested in her tactic; the work happens in her eyes)
SCENE DIRECTION (shared, unspoken): get him back.
MOTIVE (her fuel): she has been kneeling over him for a minute, frightened he would not wake up — and now he
is smiling and puckering at the sky.
GOAL: find out what is happening to him.
OBSTACLE: what is happening to him makes no sense.
TACTIC: she reads his face for the answer and finds only a pucker; the confusion is total and honest. When he
grabs her, she is too surprised to resist; she snaps his name to break it. When he lets go she recovers in
silence — the hair, the glasses — because a practical hand is how she hides her face.
Moment to moment:
— over him — frightened, then puzzled by the smile.
— the pucker — the frown; the slow head tilt.
— pulled down onto him — shock; "Ryan, what are you doing?!"
— his "sorry" — a stunned stare; she does not answer yet.
— the glasses — practical, silent; a small shake of the head.
(Safety: gaze always engaged in the task — never a frozen, glassy stare; natural blink cadence.)

ENJEE, DREAM — a dream version of her: calm, certain, tender, unhurried, the way he imagines her; she says the
line looking straight into his eyes and leans in slowly.

PHYSICS
Dream: the voile panels drift and billow in a slow warm breeze, light passing through them; the tall grass sways;
Enjee's hair lifts in soft strands; her palm rests lightly on his cheek. When the voice cuts in, the breeze stops at
once and the fabric falls still. Reality: the asphalt is hard and dark; in the top-down shot his lips push up into an
exaggerated pucker and his chin lifts; the hug has real force — Enjee's body tipped off balance, her hands
slapping down flat on the asphalt to catch herself, her hair falling around both their faces. Letting go, his arms
spring open. Sitting up is an effort: elbows, then hands, then a pause and the wince. The glasses are picked off
the asphalt and land in his palm.

LIGHTING
Dream: warm golden-hour backlight through the voile, glowing highlights on hair and fabric edges, soft peach
fill on the faces, a gentle diffusion and slightly lifted blacks — bright, tender, a little too perfect. Reality: night
lit only by the dormitory — the cyan entrance and teal window bands giving a cool spill, the asphalt falling to
near-black, faces readable with clear catchlights, the bruise reading as soft redness and swelling. The cuts
between the two worlds are hard and the contrast between warm and cool is immediate.

AUDIO
Sound effects and voices only. Dream: a soft warm wind, fabric rustling, grass whispering, everything slightly
airy and reverberant. Reality: crickets, distant traffic, Enjee's worried breathing, then the silence of her
confusion. At 15.0 the sharp real voice cuts the dream sound off completely, as if a door slammed on it. After
that, only the night: the scrape of hands on asphalt, cloth, Ryan's panicked breath, his wince, the small click of
the glasses. Only one character speaks at a time, natural spoken English.
3.0 — ENJEE (dream), soft, certain: "You're the bravest… and the best. Next to you, Chen is nobody."
15.0 — ENJEE (real), sharp, loud, cutting into the dream: "Ryan, what are you doing?!"
19.6 — RYAN, flustered, fast: "Sorry — sorry! I — sorry…"

Live-action Korean teen-drama realism with editorial fashion styling and a comic edge. Real skin texture,
natural pores. The dream is a warm, soft, romantic fantasy — golden light through sheer fabric, a meadow too

SCENE CONTEXT
The afternoon before a Halloween party. Four people, four rooms, cut together fast: Chen chivvying his crew, Jenny hunting for a costume, Enjee choosing an outfit, and finally Chen and Mark ready to go.

TWO KINDS OF CUT ARE USED IN THIS FILM, AND THEY ARE DIFFERENT
1. WHIP CUTS between locations: THE PICTURE SLIDES FROM RIGHT TO LEFT and exits the LEFT EDGE in heavy horizontal motion blur; the next shot arrives behind it from the right. This direction never reverses.
2. JUMP CUTS inside shots 2 and 3, used to change the clothes in the girls' hands. A JUMP CUT IS AN INSTANT HARD SPLICE: the camera position, the framing and the girl's pose stay exactly the same, and the garments she is holding are simply DIFFERENT in the very next frame. THE GARMENTS NEVER TRANSFORM ON SCREEN. There is no morph, no dissolve, no fade, no cross-blend, no colour sliding from one shade to another, no fabric growing, melting or reshaping. Each garment is a complete, solid, still object before the cut and a completely different complete, solid, still object after it. It must read as film spliced together, not as one garment changing.

IDENTITY LOCK
EXACTLY FIVE PEOPLE EXIST IN THIS FILM: Chen, Mark, Jenny, Enjee and one anonymous decorator. Every room is otherwise empty.
Chen is in the hall corner and his own bedroom; Mark only in Chen's bedroom; Jenny only in her wardrobe; Enjee only in her own bedroom. Each keeps one face and one outfit throughout. No face drift, no identity swap, no duplicated person.
Every face is bare and clean — plain natural skin, no make-up, no paint. The plastic fangs in shot 6 are the only costume item worn on a face.

The door is a heavy solid panel on real hinges: it needs force from inside, swings fast, strikes Chen with a flat

before the afternoon.

GOAL: have the girl brought to her, in this room, now.

talking, which hands the obligation to fill the silence to the man behind the desk. She checks his eyes once
after the question — not for agreement, for compliance — and finds it.

SCENE DIRECTION (shared, unspoken): keep it easy — nobody gets to see anybody trying.
MOTIVE (his fuel): last week in that cafeteria his body did something his rules do not allow, and he has come
